houseViews.paragraph: Key Takeaways We hosted Abhijeet Dabas (Head - Nykaa Fashion.com) and Namrata Penta (Head IR). We summarize key takeaways below. Key focus for Beauty remains customer acquisition and driving higher frequency of purchase, and for Fashion it is onboarding the right kind of customers and brands.

Nykaa reported 28% revenue growth in 4QFY26 and its highest-ever Ebitda margin of 8.4%, up 195bps YoY, with Ebitda 8% above consensus. Beauty NSV grew 29% YoY with margin-accretive own brands up 54%, driving a +70bps Ebitda margin. Fashion saw 42% YoY NSV growth with Ebitda breakeven.

NYKAA's Q4 EBITDA was ahead of our and Street's estimates. Beauty EBITDA sustained its upward trajectory while Fashion turned EBITDA positive for the first time. Beauty GMV/NSV/Revenue growth stood at 27%/29%/27%, **driven by healthy growth in transacting user base and strong growth fo**r own brands.

Nykaa posted healthy revenue growth of 28% yoy, **aided by a similar 28% yoy growth in overall GMV**. BPC reported 27% yoy growth in both GMV and revenues. Fashion reported 29% yoy growth in GMV and a higher 40% yoy revenue growth.

EBITDA margin; fashion reported continued acceleration, with break-even signalling mgmt. has cracked the code; own brands continue to go from strength to strength. The medium-term outlook is quite positive, although mgmt. sounded a note of caution in the context of a tough macro. We retain BUY despite stiff valuations, which are **supported by strong growth**.

EBITDA margin at 8.4% (Nomura: 7.6%, Bloomberg consensus: 8.1%) Nykaa's 4QFY26 revenue at INR26.5bn (+28% y-y; Fig. EBITDA margin was ahead at 8.4% leading to EBITDA of INR2.2bn, +67% y-y (11%/5% above Nomura/consensus). RM/sales was at 54.6% (Nomura: 54.8%), but marketing costs were lower at 14.3% (Nomura: 15.2%).

houseViews.paragraph: Honasa reported revenue growth of 23% YoY (28% growth ex-change in accounting) 4%/6% ahead of our estimate/consensus. Volume grew 30% while its margin expanded more than 650bps YoY, leading to a beat on Ebitda of 19%/24% versus our estimate/consensus. Three things stood out for us.

Honasa's Q4 EBITDA was ahead of our estimates, **aided by better-than-expected gross margin delivery even as revenue w**as marginally above our forecasts. Looking ahead, management **targets a high-teens revenue CAGR over the next five years**, with Mamaearth expected to deliver a double-digit CAGR **driven by distribution expansion and young brands continuing to drive **outsized growth.

Honasa's 4Q organic LFL revenue growth of 21% yoy was strong, **aided by 28% yoy growth in younger brands and mid-teen growth in the **Mamaearth brand. Adjusted EBITDA margin of 11.3% (KIE: 9.7%) was a multi-quarter high, **aided by strong operating leverage**.

Honasa is firmly on a strong growth path. Performance further improved in 4Q, with mid-teens growth at Mamaearth, continued strong momentum in younger brands, and margins reaching their highest-ever levels. Guidance of high-teens revenue growth with 100bps annual EBITDA expansion implies a compounding story is in the making, which should bring investor focus back to the name.
Steady start to the fiscal; scale and mix to drive momentum.

houseViews.paragraph: Cigarettes Ebit grew 7.2% YoY in 4QFY26 and was 15% ahead of consensus. ITC's Q4 EBITDA was 3% ahead of our estimate owing to better-than-expected profitability for Cigarettes, FMCG and Paper divisions.

ITC's 4Q EBITDA grew 7.3% yoy (KIE: 4%). Cigarette segment net revenues /EBIT grew ~10.4%/7.2% yoy in 4Q--this print does not reflect the underlying demand and profitability due to one-off realization gains in February and divergent primary/secondary sales across months amid transition to the new taxation structure.
Also, there was a change in the method of GST computation, indicating that the optical reported growth numbers are not comparable.

The impact of the sharp tax hike was only partial, but 4Q also likely benefited from pipeline inventory around the cut-off date (JEFe). However, the real test is in 1QFY27, when the impact of the sharp tax hike will be visible, as price hikes are only partial while volumes & margins will be affected. We retain HOLD with a lower PT at Rs350 - the stock is likely to stay range-bound in the near term.

houseViews.paragraph: Karan Arora (Manager, Investor Relations). Key takeaways: The company is seeing ~180bps cost pressure from inflation in LPG costs (120bps), labour cost, and commodities. Domino's has implemented a ~1.2% price hike so far.

Jubilant FoodWorks (JUBI) reported standalone sales growth of 6.4%, with 0.2% Domino's India LFL growth, as previously disclosed in its business update. The company attributed the slowdown in LFL to (1) a high base of 12.1% LFL, (2) lower AOV due to a lower minimum order value, (3) softer dine-in and takeaway growth, (4) 30-40bps of impact due to LPG unavailability and (5) the sequential occurrence of Ramadan and school examinations and the shift of Navratri. Gross margin improved by 98bps YoY.

Target (Mar-27):Rs474.00 Prior (Mar-27):Rs480.00 JUBI's Q4 pre-INDAS EBITDA growth was modest at +5% y/y, weighed down by higher rental expenses and soft revenue growth (+5% y/y; LFL +0.2%) despite betterthan-expected gross margin delivery (+100bp y/y).

Domino's India LFL growth decelerated to flat yoy (KIE: 1.5%) in 4Q due to a high base, AOV decline and dine-in weakness. EBITDA margin of 12.1% was 20 bps below our estimate, despite 40 bps GM beat, due to adverse operating leverage. JUBI called out near-term margin pressure despite a calibrated 12% price hike due to higher energy costs, increase in labor costs (minimum wage up in 11 states) and some RM inflation.

With consumer tech platforms becoming preferred ways for investors to play the consumption theme, JUBI's 4Q provided no reason to revisit the name. Flat SSS & cautious ST margin commentary suggest wait for a turnaround continues. Still, the exit trajectory results in a 10-12% cut in EBITDA as mgmt **aims for a calibrated price hike**, which we view as a prudent strategy.

houseViews.paragraph: LTIMindtree (LTM) held an analyst meeting where it shared its AI strategy around gaining market share, with the core message being to double revenue over the next five years with a 15-17% contribution from inorganic growth implying an organic revenue Cagr of 14.5%.

LTM's Analyst Day clarified its strategic direction as a repositioning from traditional tech services to a domain and tech convergence partner with AI-led services, platform-led delivery and outcome-based pricing at the centre of a new five-year plan. We saw six main takeaways: First, AI deflation is shrinking legacy work by 20-25%, with the industry already in the second year of deflation.

Lakshya goals of doubling revenue and increasing EBIT margins by 200 bps in FY2031, which is quite optimistic, in our view. The AI strategy is anchored on domain x tech convergence, reimagined capabilities (iRun, iTransform and Business AI) and the Blueverse ecosystem. The direction is sound, but several elements mirror peer strategies.

AI-led disruption could deflate core IT service revenues by c.25%, but AI will expand the addressable market by US$1.3tn, **driven by Platformized IT and Business AI services**. LTM's **plans to pivot to outcomebased offerings require a material change to pricing and talent **strategy which may not be easy to execute. In this context, its aspirations to double revenues by 2031 with 200bps margin expansion seem very optimistic.

houseViews.paragraph: HC O-PF The c.5% fall in ONGC's stock price post 4Q results appears overdone and we **see this as an added opportunity to buy**. Its 4QFY26 standalone PAT missed by 22% but the post-4Q analyst call revealed a slew of one-off charges. Adjusted for these one-off charges, core Ebit as well as PBT were inline with our estimates.
PAT of Rs.66.5bn **missed JPMe** and consensus estimates by 17/14%. Crude production for the quarter was down 6% YoY while gas output contracted 3% YoY.

KIE and EBITDA down 6.5% (~14% below KIE), **driven by weaker volumes and one-offs**. Oil/gas sales declined 5%/3% yoy (flat for FY2026), impacted by KG-98/2 delays and West Asia war. Positively, in year one of the BP TSP, MH production exceeded baseline by 2% for oil and 9% for gas despite limited capex, with likely sharper gains as new facilities come up.

Neutral with higher **TP of INR295** 4Q earnings miss due to higher expenses; volume/ realizations ahead/in line ONGC's 4QFY26 standalone net revenue at INR359bn was up 14% q-q (+3% y-y), reflecting higher crude and gas realizations q-q (Fig. Reported EBITDA of INR126.7bn fell 17% q-q (-9% y-y) on higher other expenses (up 44% q-q), and higher dry well writeoffs, +220% q-q).
Production Remains a Drag Consol Ebitda was inline while Pat was 10% lower than JEFe. Production failed to bring cheer. Drag from HPCL's loss will negate higher crude price benefit in FY27E.
Total production stood at ~6.64 MMTOE including 3.45MMT crude oil and 3.15BCM gas. Production in FY26 was impacted by Assam blockades, causing a loss of ~0.1MMT in crude and ~0.3BCM in gas.

Promoter Aditya Birla Group has agreed to infuse Rs47.3bn through a Rs4.3bn preferential warrants issue at Rs11/share with 25% of money coming in 1HFY27 and the remaining 75% over the next 18 months, supporting capex in the absence of bank funding in the short term. The government has reduced AGR due to Rs640bn from Rs877bn, with payments scheduled over FY36-41.

Vi's reported EBITDA of Rs48.9 bn was above our estimates on a combination of lower subscriber attrition and better ARPU. GoI relief on the AGR front addresses near-term funding issues, while promoter involvement via preferential issue further improves debt raising prospects. We find its threeyear EBITDA target ambitious.

ARPU trends key monitorables 4QFY26 earnings stable; subscriber loss arrested; healthy ARPU improvement VIL's 4QFY26 revenue at INR113bn was up 0.1% q-q and 2.9% y-y, reflecting a 1.2% q-q increase in ARPU to INR174, which was partly offset by net subscriber loss of 0.1mn to EoP subscribers of 192.8mn. Reported ARPU (including M2M) rose by INR2 (+1.2% q-q) in 4QFY26, while retail consumer ARPU increased at a faster pace of 2.2% q-q.
